topic: A clean restart of both servers with 10,000 tables
canonical_claim: A clean restart of both servers with 10,000 tables recovered all tables in 64.2 seconds, with no unknown-disk false positives and `CasBlobList=0` at startup; the rapid-kill S13 wedge is not a normal graceful-restart failure.

topic: Cas::listMounts enumerates mount slots with one LIST and one
canonical_claim: `Cas::listMounts` enumerates mount slots with one LIST and one GET per slot and classifies each as `live`, `expired`, `terminated`, `fenced`, or `corrupt`.; The `system.cas_mounts` `state` value is one of `live`, `expired`, `terminated`, `fenced`, or `corrupt`.

topic: The planned system.content_addressed_mounts table has columns disk, srid, server_uuid
canonical_claim: The planned `system.content_addressed_mounts` table has columns `disk`, `srid`, `server_uuid`, `hostname`, `pid`, `writer_epoch`, `seq`, `started_at_ms`, `expires_at_ms`, `min_active`, `observed_gc_round`, `gc_fenced`, and `state`.

topic: Mount-slot audit adds CasEventType::MountClaim, MountRelease, and MountConflict, serialized as
canonical_claim: Mount-slot audit adds `CasEventType::MountClaim`, `MountRelease`, and `MountConflict`, serialized as `mount_claim`, `mount_release`, and `mount_conflict`; conflict details include the observed holder UUID, hostname, PID, epoch, sequence, and expiry when available.

topic: Store::observedGcRound() returns the currently installed retire_view.round() through the retired
canonical_claim: `Store::observedGcRound()` returns the currently installed `retire_view.round()` through the retired view's internal synchronization, so renewal performs local reads and one lease PUT without a `gc/state` GET. `Store::observedGcRound() const` returns `retire_view.round()` as a cheap, race-safe in-memory read, and `renewLeaseOnlyForTest()` renews without synchronizing the retired view.; The retired-view syncer runs `syncRetiredView()` every `mount_renew_period`, performs the `gc/state` probe and `RetireView::refresh()` only when the published round is newer, and emits `RetiredViewAdvance` only for an actual advance.; The lease/view decoupling moves S3-heavy retired-view refresh off `MountLeaseKeeper::renewOnce`; renewal reads only cheap in-memory values including `Store::observedGcRound()`, while a Store-owned poller runs `Store::syncRetiredView()` independently. The lease/view implementation splits the merged heartbeat into a cheap renewal path using `Store::observedGcRound()` and a Store-owned `syncRetiredView` poller that performs the S3-heavy work independently. Mount lease renewal no longer performs the S3-heavy retired-view refresh; it reads `Store::observedGcRound`, while a dedicated `syncRetiredView` thread advances the view so object-store latency cannot block renewal past the TTL.

topic: Both the lease-renewal thread and retired-view syncer are gated
canonical_claim: Both the lease-renewal thread and retired-view syncer are gated by `background_watermark`; `Store::open` and `tryRemountOnce` synchronously call `syncRetiredView()` before starting the keeper so the first anchored lease carries a current acknowledgement.

topic: The retired-view syncer catches and logs its own exceptions
canonical_claim: The retired-view syncer catches and logs its own exceptions, retries on the next tick, and must be stopped and joined before `retire_view` or `pool_backend` are destroyed; renewal fail-closed behavior otherwise remains unchanged.

topic: Terminating a never-started SingleWriterSlot is a quiet no-op, while
canonical_claim: Terminating a never-started `SingleWriterSlot` is a quiet no-op, while double termination of a genuinely started slot remains an exception. `SingleWriterSlot::doTerminate` is a quiet no-op when `seq == 0`, because a keeper whose start never succeeded has nothing to release; double termination remains an exception.; A `LOGICAL_ERROR` "release before start" fires when Store teardown calls `stop()`/`doTerminate` on a mount-lease keeper whose `seq` is still 0 because `doStart` threw before completing; this is pure noise during an already-failing shutdown rather than a real defect signal, and the recommended fix is for `doTerminate` with `seq == 0` to be a quiet no-op.

topic: After a successful mount claim, doStart retains one synchronous
canonical_claim: After a successful mount claim, `doStart` retains one synchronous view refresh before the first lease body; the renewal background path itself is a single lease PUT and the view refresh runs on its own cadence.

topic: Store::renewWatermarkOnce() remains the composed test/manual driver that runs syncRetiredView()
canonical_claim: `Store::renewWatermarkOnce()` remains the composed test/manual driver that runs `syncRetiredView()` and then `mount_keeper->renewOnce()`, while production renewal uses the isolated cheap path.

topic: The Store-owned retired-view syncer exposes startRetiredViewSync, idempotent...
canonical_claim: The Store-owned retired-view syncer exposes `startRetiredViewSync`, idempotent `stopRetiredViewSync`, and `retiredViewSyncLoop`; it waits on a condition variable, catches and logs body exceptions, and is joined during Store teardown.

topic: A foreign server_uuid causes a fail-closed refusal, while an
canonical_claim: A foreign `server_uuid` causes a fail-closed refusal, while an own UUID with `gc_fenced` is a recoverable fence state and an own UUID with a newer unfenced epoch is a fail-closed supersession.

topic: prepareRenew must be O(1) and use the last installed
canonical_claim: `prepareRenew` must be O(1) and use the last installed `retire_view.round()` acknowledgement plus `minActive()` without running the beat; the beat runs on a separate cadence.

topic: A fence-recovery implementation must classify same-UUID fenced bodies as
canonical_claim: A fence-recovery implementation must classify same-UUID fenced bodies as recoverable, decouple the beat from the renewal deadline, retry cold-open claim/adopt, and make `doTerminate` with `seq == 0` a no-op.

topic: The P3.1 fence-recovery cycle recovered a fenced ch1 mount
canonical_claim: The P3.1 fence-recovery cycle recovered a fenced ch1 mount in about two seconds as `writer_epoch=2`, `seq=1`, `gc_fenced=0`, and `state=live`, with no post-kill foreign-writer or exit-49 lines.

topic: CA metadata startup() and shutdown() are idempotent, allowing the
canonical_claim: CA metadata `startup()` and `shutdown()` are idempotent, allowing the base disk and cache disk to share one CA mount and one lease when they reuse the same metadata storage.

topic: The writer-side RetireView, its syncer, observed_gc_round, and ack-floor are
canonical_claim: The writer-side `RetireView`, its syncer, `observed_gc_round`, and ack-floor are removed; `MountLease` loses `observed_gc_round`, the beat publishes only `{now, min_active}`, and GC round recovery no longer uses `min_ack` or `max_ack`.; The build watermark min_active is carried in the mount lease; the standalone watermark object and writer-side observed_gc_round retired-view machinery were removed. Liveness and the `min_active` build-watermark floor are carried in one `MountLeaseKeeper` slot.; Each server maintains one merged heartbeat object at `gc/server-roots/<srid>/mount`, replacing the separate `roots/<server-hex>/_watermark` object and `WatermarkKeeper`.

topic: The writer records an exact precommit removal before retiring
canonical_claim: The writer records an exact precommit removal before retiring a failed build, while a newly mounted writer fences the predecessor epoch and appends one constant-size epoch clear per affected namespace.

topic: A writer does not retire a build while it
canonical_claim: A writer does not retire a build while it owns a precommit; if the process stops first, only a successor that fenced the entire predecessor epoch may append the namespace-scoped epoch clear.

topic: WriterId is { writer_epoch, writer_sequence }, both components are
canonical_claim: `WriterId` is `{ writer_epoch, writer_sequence }`, both components are nonzero `UInt64` values, each successful mount strictly increases `writer_epoch`, and `writer_sequence` starts at one within an epoch.

topic: A current-build precommit removal requires the build to remain
canonical_claim: A current-build precommit removal requires the build to remain locally active until the exact removal record is durable; the replay transition is not liveness-dependent. For a current-writer failure, the writer keeps the build active, appends the exact precommit removal, and retires the build only after that removal is durable; if the append fails, the build remains active and the error propagates.

topic: Writable startup fences the predecessor, verifies the exact adopted
canonical_claim: Writable startup fences the predecessor, verifies the exact adopted fold seal, installs its `RefBaseSet` metadata, and lazily loads each namespace by reading its base rows and replaying its complete tail between before/after `gc/state` checks.

topic: Artifact keys are pinned to attempt = lease.seq, and
canonical_claim: Artifact keys are pinned to `attempt = lease.seq`, and renew or steal paths bump `lease.seq` every round, so a same-key collision can only be a byte-identical resend within the same attempt.

topic: RefTxnId is { writer_epoch: UInt64, ref_sequence: UInt64 }; both
canonical_claim: `RefTxnId` is `{ writer_epoch: UInt64, ref_sequence: UInt64 }`; both fields are nonzero, writer epochs strictly increase on successful mounts, and `ref_sequence` is strictly increasing within a mounted writer epoch.

topic: Namespace recreation after remove_namespace requires the _cleanup/<remove-txn-id> marker for
canonical_claim: Namespace recreation after `remove_namespace` requires the `_cleanup/<remove-txn-id>` marker for the exact removal transaction; an empty physical prefix is not sufficient. The writer consumes only the `_cleanup/<remove-txn-id>` marker as the namespace cleanup completion signal; a physically empty prefix is not authoritative.

topic: If a mount lease expires, the writer is fenced
canonical_claim: If a mount lease expires, the writer is fenced and a subsequent staging-source 404 must fail closed by aborting the insert rather than committing.

topic: The staging sweeper exposes sweepOwnMountOnStart() and ageSweep(now, ttl), both
canonical_claim: The staging sweeper exposes `sweepOwnMountOnStart()` and `ageSweep(now, ttl)`, both lease-fenced so an in-flight staging object younger than TTL is not deleted.

topic: CAS separates attempt_timeout, operation_deadline, and the local lease_deadline; a
canonical_claim: CAS separates `attempt_timeout`, `operation_deadline`, and the local `lease_deadline`; a writer attempt requires an unfenced mount, `now < lease_deadline`, `now + attempt_timeout + lease_safety_margin < lease_deadline`, and `now + attempt_timeout <= operation_deadline`.

topic: lease_safety_margin accounts for local scheduling delay, timeout granularity, and
canonical_claim: `lease_safety_margin` accounts for local scheduling delay, timeout granularity, and configured clock-skew allowance, but does not bound server-side completion after a client timeout.

topic: A writer updates its cache and returns ACK only
canonical_claim: A writer updates its cache and returns ACK only after a fence check, one controlled S3 attempt, permitted resolution, and a final fence check; if the final check fails, it returns no ACK and reports uncertainty when the object may exist.
